newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps all bounce higher as crude leads.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps all bounce higher as crude leads.

text.p: European oil swaps bounded higher on Tuesday as crude lead the charge on the back of tight wet barrels.
Brent CFDs galloped ahead gaining over 20 cents, gasoline bounced up $3 with support from tomorrow's U.K. budget, naphtha tracked crude making $3 or so while fuel edged up 75 cents to $1.

Dealers said Brent CFDs for the balance of this week jumped to August flat compared with -22 cents on Monday and Tuesday morning. July 7-11 CFDs were also stronger with -2/3 cents against August Brent talked from -28 cents. July 14-18 was put at -8/9 cents from -30 cents and July 21-25 was assessed at -10 from -30 cents.
The drive for higher numbers came when July/August spread was done at +10 cents against -2.5 at the end of Monday.
Several CFDs were done with July 7-11 trading at - 9 cents, -1 cent and -7 cents against August while 21-25 went at -23 against September. July 28-August 1 was sold at -30 cents against September.
Heavy fuel oil swaps were 75 cents to $1 higher, but activity was understood to have been slow. July was pegged at $83.75-84.25, August at $84.75 and September at $85.25.
The high-low spread against low sulphur swaps was close to $11 on July but down to $7.75 on Q4. Dealers said strength in the U.S. was bouying low sulphur swaps to $1 gains.
Gasoline swaps were about $3 stronger and much busier as dealers anticipated the U.K. budget on Wednesday to increase excise duties.
Some wet tightness in Rotterdam also helped. Traders said July swaps traded between $185.75 and $187.75 while August traded bewteen $185.75 and $187.75.
Naphtha was also about $3 firmer with an August swaps trading at $179.
